analysis: Seven analyses requested as 'what would a PI push on'. All exploratory, none pre-registered, all from data already on disk. No new compute.

E2_the_proposals_own_mechanism_experimen.status: RUN AT LAST - it had been listed as not run in every prior draft
E2_the_proposals_own_mechanism_experimen.method: All 35 four-member panels from the 7 reward models. For each: mean individual AUROC (quality), mean pairwise correlation of errors (rank-normalised score minus gold), and AUROC(u).
E2_the_proposals_own_mechanism_experimen.proposal_predicted: strongly negative: decorrelated errors should buy residual detection value
E2_the_proposals_own_mechanism_experimen.finding: Two things, and the first is the more important. (1) There is no decorrelated panel to be had: every one of the 35 panels has pairwise error correlation between 0.71 and 0.89. The diversity knob the proposal assumed exists does not turn for off-the-shelf critics. (2) Within that narrow range, error correlation does not predict AUROC(u) - the partial correlation is -0.11 and +0.08, opposite signs across benchmarks and both near zero. The mechanism the proposal named cannot be exercised, and where it can be varied slightly it does nothing.

LC_is_it_disagreement_or_the_panel.method: Feed the four raw panel scores to a learned combiner instead of only their spread, out of fold.
LC_is_it_disagreement_or_the_panel.finding: The four raw scores do not beat their spread on either benchmark under the assumption-free estimator. The claim strengthens: it is not that disagreement is the wrong function of the panel - on the committed population the panel carries nothing to extract.

CD_candidate_diversity.finding: The four candidates are genuinely different patches, sharing 18-22% of changed lines. So Amendment 4f's result - that selection did not concentrate failure - is NOT explained by the selector having nothing to choose between. It had real choices and still did not concentrate failure.

TB_agent_self_verification.finding: Whether the agent verified its own work barely predicts silent failure (0.52 on the benchmark where it varies). On Verified every trajectory ran a test, so the feature has no variance there. This contradicts the intuition that behavioural signals should work on this population.

CAL_judge_calibration.finding: Every judge is overconfident. Stated resolve probabilities average 0.66-0.84 against actual rates of 0.55-0.65; ECE runs 0.16-0.34. Several judges have Brier scores at or above 0.25, which is what you get by always saying 50%. gpt-6-luna is the most overconfident (says 0.84, actual 0.65) while being among the best rankers. Judges rank moderately and know poorly.

E3_selection_pressure.finding: No consistent pressure effect. The proposal predicted the null would deepen as n grows; it deepens on one benchmark and is flat on the other.

XB_cross_benchmark_transfer.finding: Nothing transfers. Every model fitted on one benchmark scores 0.50-0.56 on the other, whether built from structure, from the critic scores, or from disagreement alone.

what_remains_unexamined: Failure taxonomy (proposal E5): what kinds of silent failure these are, and whether any class is detectable. Needs labelling ~47 failures.
Lucky passes: AgentLens reports 10.7% of passing SWE trajectories pass by accident; our g=1 labels have never been checked for this.
Other domains (proposal E6): WebArena/ALFWorld. Genuinely expensive; recommended dropped.
